title: Trigonometry: From Right to Oblique Triangles Exit Ticket
description: Checkpoint on distinguishing triangle types and classifying given triangle-solving cases.

questions.question: A triangle has one angle measuring exactly 90 degrees. Which classification should you choose first?
questions.explanation: The exact 90-degree angle makes it a right triangle before any other solving case is considered.

questions.question: A triangle has angles 54 degrees, 58 degrees, and 68 degrees. Which classification is most precise?
questions.explanation: None of the angles is 90 degrees, so the triangle is oblique. All angles are acute, so it is an acute oblique triangle.

questions.question: A triangle has angles 18 degrees, 47 degrees, and 115 degrees. Which classification is most precise?
questions.explanation: The triangle has no 90-degree angle, so it is oblique. The 115-degree angle makes it obtuse.

questions.question: In triangle ABC, angles A and B are known, and side AB is also known. Side AB lies between the two known angles. Which case is this?
questions.explanation: Two angles with the included side form ASA.

questions.question: In triangle ABC, angles A and B are known, and side AC is known. Side AC is not between the two known angles. Which case is this?
questions.explanation: Two angles and a non-included side form AAS.

questions.question: A triangle has side lengths 9 cm and 13 cm, and the angle between those sides is 71 degrees. Which case is this?
questions.explanation: The known angle is included between the two known sides, so the case is SAS.

questions.question: A triangle has side lengths 8 cm and 12 cm, and a known angle that is not between those two sides. Which case is this?
questions.explanation: Two known sides and a non-included angle form SSA.

questions.question: A triangle has sides 6 m, 10 m, and 12 m known. Which case is this?
questions.explanation: All three side lengths are known, so the case is SSS.

questions.question: AAS and ASA both involve two known angles, but ASA uses the included side while AAS uses a non-included side.
questions.explanation: The difference between ASA and AAS is the position of the known side.

questions.question: A student sees a triangle with no 90-degree angle and immediately uses right-triangle sine, cosine, and tangent. In one or two sentences, explain the mistake.
questions.correctAnswer: Right-triangle sine, cosine, and tangent ratios directly apply to right triangles. A triangle with no 90-degree angle is oblique, so the student should first identify the given case and then consider tools such as the Law of Sines or Law of Cosines.
questions.explanation: The key idea is that right-triangle trig depends on a right angle; oblique triangles need a different starting plan.

questions.question: Classify this situation and explain briefly: A triangle has two sides given and the angle between them given.
questions.correctAnswer: The case is SAS because the known angle is included between the two known sides.
questions.explanation: A complete answer names SAS and uses the word included or explains that the angle is between the known sides.
